parts.latex:
A regular hexagon of side length 5 cm is shown below.

\exfigure{717_q30_1}

The hexagon has been divided into two triangles $AEF$ and $BDC$, and a rectangle $ABDE$, as shown above.

Show that the area of the hexagon is approximately $65\text{ cm}^2$.

solutions.latex:
Each interior angle of a regular hexagon is $120^\circ$, so $\angle AFE=120^\circ$.

Using the cosine rule in $\triangle AEF$:
$$\begin{aligned} AE^2 &= 5^2+5^2-2\times 5\times 5\times\cos 120^\circ \\ &= 25+25-50\cos 120^\circ \\ &= 75 \end{aligned}$$
$$AE \approx 8.7 \text{ cm}$$
Area of $\triangle AEF$:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2}\times 5\times 5\times\sin 120^\circ \\ &\approx 10.8 \text{ cm}^2 \end{aligned}$$
Area of rectangle $ABDE$:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= 8.7\times 5 \\ &= 43.5 \text{ cm}^2 \end{aligned}$$
The hexagon is two triangles plus the rectangle.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Area of hexagon} &= (2\times 10.8)+43.5 \\ &\approx 65 \text{ cm}^2 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the areas of the triangle and the rectangle, or equivalent merit
Finds $\angle AFE$ or sets up the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Both triangles share the angle $A$, so use the area formula with two sides and the included angle.
$$\text{Area}_{\triangle ABC} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 4 \times \sin A = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 12 \times \sin A$$

figures.cap: quadrilateral ABCD with diagonal BD
solution sketch: quadrilateral with angles marked

solutions.latex:
Split the quadrilateral into triangles $ABD$ and $BCD$ using diagonal $BD$.

\exfigure{714_q29_s1}

In right-angled triangle $ABD$, by Pythagoras' theorem:
$$BD^2 = 6^2 + 9.5^2$$
$$BD = \sqrt{126.25}$$
In triangle $BCD$, by the cosine rule:
$$\cos \angle BCD = \dfrac{15.61^2 + 10^2 - \left(\sqrt{126.25}\right)^2}{2 \times 15.61 \times 10}$$
$$\angle BCD = 45.859^\circ = 45^\circ 51' \approx 46^\circ$$
The area is the sum of the two triangles.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 9.5 \times 6 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 15.61 \times 10 \times \sin 45.859^\circ \\ &= 84.511\ldots \\ &\approx 84.5 \text{ km}^2 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds $\angle BCD$ and sets up the area of both triangles, or equivalent merit
Finds $BD$ and sets up the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

7372.stem:
The diagram below shows an isosceles triangle $XYZ$ with $XZ = XY = k$, $YZ = 10$ cm and angle $YXZ = \theta$.

\exfigure{235_q36_1}

figures.cap: isosceles triangle XYZ with XY = XZ = k, YZ = 10 cm, angle theta at X

parts.latex: By considering the area of the triangle, show that $\sin\theta = \dfrac{10\sqrt{k^2-25}}{k^2}$.
Given that the area of the triangle is $60\ \text{cm}^2$, find the size of $\theta$ correct to the nearest degree.

solutions.latex:
Draw the perpendicular from $X$ to the midpoint $M$ of $YZ$ (the triangle is isosceles, so this bisects $YZ$). Then $YM = 5$.

In right-angled triangle $XMY$, by Pythagoras' theorem:
$$XM = \sqrt{k^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{k^2 - 25}$$
Area using base $YZ$ and height $XM$:
$$A = \dfrac{1}{2}\times 10\times\sqrt{k^2 - 25} = 5\sqrt{k^2 - 25}$$
Area using two sides and the included angle, $A = \dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$:
$$A = \dfrac{1}{2}k^2\sin\theta$$
Equate the two areas:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{1}{2}k^2\sin\theta &= 5\sqrt{k^2 - 25} \\ \sin\theta &= \dfrac{10\sqrt{k^2 - 25}}{k^2} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Writes both area expressions, or equivalent merit
Finds the height $\sqrt{k^2 - 25}$ and one area expression, or equivalent merit
Finds the height $\sqrt{k^2 - 25}$, or equivalent merit

meta.generated_note: Written by us; no source solution.

solutions.latex:
From part (a), the area is $5\sqrt{k^2 - 25}$. Set it equal to $60$:
$$\begin{aligned} 5\sqrt{k^2 - 25} &= 60 \\ \sqrt{k^2 - 25} &= 12 \\ k^2 - 25 &= 144 \\ k^2 &= 169 \end{aligned}$$
So $k = 13$ (a length is positive). Then
$$\sin\theta = \dfrac{10\times 12}{169} = \dfrac{120}{169}$$
$$\theta \approx 45.2^\circ \text{ or } 134.8^\circ$$
The perpendicular $XM$ bisects $\theta$, so in triangle $XMY$:
$$\sin\dfrac{\theta}{2} = \dfrac{5}{13}$$
and so $\dfrac{\theta}{2} \approx 22.6^\circ$, which is less than $45^\circ$. Hence $\theta$ is acute, and $134.8^\circ$ is rejected.
$$\therefore\ \theta \approx 45^\circ$$

A radial survey of a paddock $KPRS$ is drawn below, showing the following information.

The distances are $OP = 38$m, $OR = 29$m, $OS = 36$m and $OK = 35$m,

The bearings $P$, $R$, $S$ and $K$ from $O$ are $093^\circ$, $187^\circ$, $238^\circ$ and $325^\circ$.

figures.cap: radial survey of paddock KPRS from point O with distances and bearings

parts.latex: Show that $\angle KOP = 128^\circ$.
Calculate the length of $KP$ to 1 decimal place.
Calculate the area of triangle $KOP$ to the nearest $\text{m}^2$.

solutions.latex:
The bearing of $K$ is $325^\circ$, so $K$ is $360^\circ - 325^\circ = 35^\circ$ west of north.
$$\begin{aligned} \angle KOP &= 35^\circ + 93^\circ \\ &= 128^\circ \end{aligned}$$

Using the cosine rule in triangle $KOP$, with $x = KP$:
$$\begin{aligned} x^2 &= 35^2 + 38^2 - 2 \times 35 \times 38 \times \cos 128^\circ \\ &= 4306.7\ldots \\ x &\approx 65.6 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Substitutes correctly into the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex: $$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 35 \times 38 \times \sin 128^\circ \\ &\approx 524 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Substitutes correctly into the area formula, or equivalent merit

The distance of $CH$ is 400 m, $DH$ is 500m and the area of the shaded acute angled triangle $CHD$ is $71\,934\ \text{m}^2$.

Calculate the bearing of bus stop $C$ from the house $H$ to the nearest degree.

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{498_q14_s1}

Using the area formula for triangle $CHD$:
$$71\,934 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 400 \times 500 \times \sin\theta$$
$$\sin\theta = \dfrac{71\,934}{100\,000}$$
The triangle is acute, so
$$\theta = \sin^{-1}(0.71934) \approx 46^\circ$$
Then the bearing of $C$ is
$$338^\circ - 46^\circ = 292^\circ$$

figures.cap: equilateral triangle poster (95 cm sides) and sector poster (radius 85 cm, angle theta)

parts.latex: Show that the area of Pablo's poster is approximately $3\,908\ \text{cm}^2$.
Find the value of $\theta$, the angle in the sector, in Claude's poster.

solutions.latex:
Pablo's poster is an equilateral triangle of side 95 cm, with each angle $60^\circ$. Using the area formula $A=\dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2}\times 95\times 95\times \sin 60^\circ \\ &= 3907.9396\ldots \\ &\approx 3908 \text{ cm}^2 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Uses the correct formula and substitution (ignore absent or wrong units)

meta.corrected: Corrected from source: $\tfrac12\times95^2\sin60^\circ$ was written $3907.9896$; it is $3907.9396$ ($3908$ unchanged).
meta.overwritten_from_source: Corrected from source: $\tfrac12\times95^2\sin60^\circ$ was written $3907.9896$; it is $3907.9396$ ($3908$ unchanged).

solutions.latex:
Using the sector area formula with radius 85 cm and area $3908 \text{ cm}^2$:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Area} &= \dfrac{\theta}{360^\circ}\times \pi r^2 \\ 3908 &= \dfrac{\theta}{360^\circ}\times \pi\times 85^2 \\ \theta &= \dfrac{3908\times 360^\circ}{\pi\times 85^2} \\ &= 61.98254\ldots \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \theta \approx 62^\circ \text{ (to the nearest degree)}$$
criteria: Achieves the equation, or equivalent merit
